regiment_total.documented_secondary_reconstruction: about 81 tanks: 5 Shinhoto Type97, 41 old-turret Type97, 35 Type95
regiment_total.USMC_operational_structure: May-15 table gives 3rd/4th/5th companies each 11 medium + 3 light; HQ 3 medium + 3 light. A 6th company was added after the table and split between Saipan/Guam.
regiment_total.interpretation: whole-regiment physical strength around 78-85 is consistent with both the company TOE and Guam/Saipan combat returns; exact model split is less secure than the total.

Saipan_strength_conflict.individual_vehicle_reconstruction: 47 9th-Regiment tanks is often cited for Saipan, with 4 Shinhoto +31 old Type97 +12 Type95.
Saipan_strength_conflict.USMC_D_day_and_night_attack: 4th Company had 14 tanks on D-Day and only 3 operative afterward; nevertheless about 44 9th-Regiment tanks were mustered for the 16/17 June attack.
Saipan_strength_conflict.reverse_inference: 44 attack-ready/theoretical + 11 lost from 4th Company implies roughly 55 9th-Regiment tanks before the D-Day loss gate, before adding naval armor.
Saipan_strength_conflict.working_resolution: Use 50-56 physical 9th-Regiment tanks on Saipan as the hard working band. Treat 47 as a lower documented-identification series and ~55 as the operational-TOE series.

Guam_crosscheck.US_Army_history: 1st Co 12-15 light tanks; 2nd Co 12-14 tanks mostly medium. Together about 24-29 9th-Regiment tanks, with a separate 29th Division tank company bringing Guam total toward the high 30s.
Guam_crosscheck.effect: A whole-regiment total around 80 is physically credible.

transfer_clock.historical_reassignment: 9th Tank Regiment removed from 1st Tank Division / reassigned to 31st Army in March 1944.
transfer_clock.historical_transport: Higashi-Matsu No.4 left Tokyo 1 April; Saipan-bound group arrived 9-10 April. Convoy suffered submarine attacks but the Saipan tank lift was not centered as lost.
transfer_clock.split: 1st and 2nd Companies plus part of a later company to Guam; 3rd/4th/5th and HQ/main remainder to Saipan.

branch_decision_clock.HAILSTONE: Branch Truk raid closes 21 Feb 1944 and demonstrates Truk can no longer act as a safe fleet/logistic concentration hub.
branch_decision_clock.organizational_background: Triangularization already creates an independent reason to detach 9th Regiment from 1st Tank Division.
branch_decision_clock.assessment: Only modestly different from historical March timing; HAILSTONE confirms rather than invents the Marianas transfer.
branch_decision_clock.embarkation: Keep East-Pine/Higashi-Matsu No.4 scale and early-April convoy clock centered. No magical March arrival.

model_mix_before_final_staging.explanation: Branch 1942-43 conversion/production gives 1st Tank Division a materially higher 47mm share than historical 9th Regiment, but no all-Shinhoto rearmament.

logic: Marianas becomes high-priority after GALVANIC + HAILSTONE.
January-February anti-Allied-medium-tank guidance makes 47mm Shinhoto preferable to 57mm old-turret tanks for this mission.
57mm HE-support vehicles remain useful and are not all discarded.
Vehicle count is held near the regiment's existing envelope; model substitution is paid from Home/depot stocks.

transport_and_arrival.reason: The historical convoy's submarine losses did not center on the Saipan tank cargo; Branch ASW does not justify inventing extra losses or perfect immunity.
transport_and_arrival.post_unload_serviceability: 90-96% within 5-10 days because vehicles receive maintenance after sea transport.

island_split_branch_center.reason: Saipan receives most medium companies; Guam receives a light-heavy 1st Company plus a medium 2nd Company.

Saipan_other_armor.guard: These are separate from the 9th Tank Regiment and must not disappear inside its count.

Saipan_15_Jun_revised_opening.comparison_to_current_settlement: Current 52-55 ready is likely low by about 4-9 vehicles, and especially understates the Branch 47mm Shinhoto share.

not_granted: 75mm turreted stopgap tank on Saipan at opening
free additional hulls from Branch production
